tool_input.command: npm test 2>&1 | tail -12; echo exit=$?; git status --short
tool_input.description: Run tests and check changed files

result:
I added `parseRanges(text, pageCount)`, and `npm test` passes: 13 tests, none failed, skipped or marked todo. Every item on the review checklist is met.

**What I changed:**
- **`src/parse-ranges.mjs`** (new): exports `parseRanges`.
  - A `text` that isn't a string, or a `pageCount` that isn't a positive integer, throws a `TypeError`.
  - It splits the text on commas. Each part must be one page (`7`) or a range (`1-3`).
  - A part that is neither, a page outside 1 to `pageCount`, or a backwards range throws a `RangeError`.
- **`tests/parse-ranges.test.mjs`** (new): covers both examples from the task (`"1-3,5"` → `[1, 2, 3, 5]` and `"7"` → `[7]` in a 10-page document) and every error case the checklist lists. It also checks the first and last page and the cases below.
- **`README.md`**: documents `parseRanges` right after `paperSize`, with an example and what throws each error.
- **`REVIEW.md`** (new): goes through the checklist item by item and gives the file and line that meets each one, as the checklist asks.

Nothing outside `src/`, `tests/`, `README.md` and `REVIEW.md` changed.

**Decisions the task left open** (these are in the README and `REVIEW.md`):
- Spaces around pages and dashes are allowed, so `" 1 - 3 , 5 "` works.
- The result lists each page once, in ascending order: `"5,1-3,2"` gives `[1, 2, 3, 5]`.
- An empty text, an empty part (`"1,,3"`) and a backwards range (`"3-1"`) all throw a `RangeError`.
- Only plain digits count as a page, so `+2`, `1e1`, `0x2` and `1.5` are refused.
